title: SITREP-EF-015: The President rejects Iran's seven-day plan, keeps the blockade, and by the Journal's account expects to resume bombing after the midterms; the Houthis end their lull with drones at Riyadh and a missile at Khamis Mushait; Brent settles at $104.32 with the Brent-WTI spread at its widest since May; the pause reaches eighteen days

SITREP-EF-014: Tehran puts a written road map on the table, a 60-day regionwide ceasefire and a phased reopening of Hormuz for the end of the blockade, with a four-to-five-day clock from Rezaei; Pezeshkian says Iran wants a deal before the midterms; Brent settles at $106.60 on the phased-deal report; Netanyahu tells the Assembly Iran's military was crushed as delegations walk out

SITREP-EF-013: Pezeshkian tells the Assembly Iran will never bow or bend the knee and will not open Hormuz while the blockade and sanctions stand, Rubio calls the talks a conversation and not a breakthrough with the June memorandum no longer on the table, Brent snaps five losing sessions at $103.08, and the pause reaches sixteen days

SITREP-EF-012: The President tells the Assembly he will deal or annihilate and expects a deal after the midterms, Witkoff and Kushner spend three hours with the Iranian delegation through mediators as Tehran offers to reopen Hormuz within days for the blockade, Saudi Arabia restarts the East-West pipeline, and Brent settles below $100

SITREP-EF-011: The President addresses the General Assembly and meets the Gulf leaders today after reportedly deciding against striking the Houthis and saying he would probably meet Iran's president, Qatar confirms messages are passing, Brent settles at $100.34, Washington moves to ground every Iranian airline, and Iran holds its fire a fourteenth day

SITREP-EF-010: A tanker entering Hormuz is hit with two crew injured on the morning the General Assembly gathers, the IRGC says it is ready for a counteroffensive and Tehran promises weapons the world will be astonished by, Iranian MPs file an NPT withdrawal bill, and the President meets the Gulf leaders tomorrow with the pause on its thirteenth day

SITREP-EF-009: The Houthis fire a ballistic missile at Riyadh and set a fuel depot burning at the capital's airport, Tehran delivers seven conditions through Qatar and warns of continuous and painful attacks on US bases if Washington resumes strikes with a regional green light, and the President meets six Gulf leaders in two days

SITREP-EF-008: The IRGC strikes a Togo-flagged tanker in Hormuz and a second tanker is hit by an unknown projectile as Saudi barrels flow out through the strait at 2.8 million a day, Brent falls a fourth session to $103.87, thousands rally for the Houthis in Sanaa, and Iran holds its fire an eleventh day before the General Assembly

SITREP-EF-007: The President says he faces a decision on whether to annihilate the Iranian regime and will hear the Gulf leaders Tuesday, Russia and China veto the sanctions panel, a UN mission finds US war crimes at Minab, and the Houthis kill their first person in Saudi Arabia this month

SITREP-EF-006: The Houthis publish video of a downed Saudi F-15, the President says the war is toward the end and that Washington deals with Tehran directly, the Fed raises rates for the first time since 2023, and the Security Council votes today on the Iran sanctions panel
SITREP-EF-005: CENTCOM confirms it destroyed two IRGC boats, a Houthi drone reaches Mecca's airspace and the movement claims Yanbu, and Saudi Red Sea loadings stop as Brent settles at $108.75
SITREP-EF-004: CENTCOM attributes the El Gaia strikes to Iran, Riyadh answers the Houthis from the air, and Treasury designates VTB as Brent closes at $108
SITREP-EF-002: Salalah ministerial postponed hours before convening as an Iranian vessel burns off Qeshm and the fire pause enters a fifth day

SIGACT-HF-015: Belleville police declare the Yom Kippur shooting a deliberate, hate-motivated attempted mass-casualty attack on the Jewish community, correcting the series' record; Sukkot's first day and the Assembly's close pass without a US incident; the President rejects Iran's plan and the Guards promise punishment until their conditions are met

SIGACT-HF-014: More than 100 arrested outside the UN during Netanyahu's address with no casualty incident as the Assembly's third day passes, Sukkot begins tonight with the allied record at three cases, Xi's state visit closes, and Iran's president denies from New York that Tehran seeks to assassinate the President

SIGACT-HF-013: The Assembly's second day passes with a US walkout during Pezeshkian's address and a Free Iran crowd outside, Xi Jinping opens a three-day state visit in Washington after bomb and death threats around a Flushing anti-Communist Party march, Netanyahu speaks today promising surprises, and the Los Angeles freeway sign stays unattributed

SIGACT-HF-012: A hacked Los Angeles freeway sign displays an IRGC-linked site that names Iranian dissidents, the Assembly's first day passes with a suspicious-package evacuation blocks from the UN and thousands rallying against the Iranian delegation, the Belleville gunman dies without a stated motive, and British police arrest two over a plot against Jews in the north of England

SIGACT-HF-011: A gunman with a shotgun opened fire on the police officer guarding a synagogue in Belleville, Ontario, as 25 congregants sat down to Kol Nidre; the United States passed Yom Kippur with no reported incident; the General Assembly opens with an Iranian delegation in New York and Washington choosing diplomacy over strikes

SIGACT-HF-010: Yom Kippur passes its first night without a reported incident in the United States as Israel stands on alert, the General Assembly gathers with an Iranian delegation and a presidential strike decision pending, and Tehran widens its retaliation language to without limitations while naming no Homeland target

SIGACT-HF-009: The FBI affidavit shows Kramer wrote of injecting ricin or cyanide into food and drink at synagogues, published as Yom Kippur begins; the FBI Director reports a 100 percent rise in specific Iran-based threats to the Homeland; Tehran names US bases and interests in the region as targets if strikes resume

SIGACT-HF-008: Yom Kippur begins at sunset tomorrow after a synagogue arson attempt in Germany, the Kramer affidavit contains a general reference to synagogues, an Iranian delegation and a presidential decision on strikes converge on the General Assembly, and no NTAS bulletin is in force

SIGACT-HF-007: Yom Kippur is two days out with no NTAS bulletin in force, an Iranian delegation is confirmed for the General Assembly as the President weighs annihilating the regime, Sweden finds Iran used criminal networks against Jewish and Israeli targets, and US agencies track cyber threats to nearly 20 vessels

SIGACT-HF-006: DHS warns that Iranian cyber actors are targeting the tank gauges of US fuel storage, an ISIS-K conspirator in the 2021 Kabul airport bombing gets 20 years, and Yom Kippur is three days out with no NTAS bulletin in force

SIGACT-HF-005: A Russian intelligence network is charged with a murder-for-hire plot against a dissident in the Washington area, an ISIS-inspired rifle plot is disrupted in Pennsylvania, and the Russia vector moves to ELEVATED
SIGACT-HF-004: Iran physical baseline corrected to a charged 2026 proxy plot; no new Homeland incident; posture ELEVATED with Yom Kippur in 6 days
SIGACT-HF-002: Rosh Hashanah and the 9/11 anniversary close without incident; Iran cyber holds HIGH; state threat charge against a US Senate candidate enters the election window
